The assistant's solution correctly computes the median using a divide-and-conquer approach (finding the k-th element). However, the implementation uses Python list slicing (`nums1[i:]`, `nums2[j:]`), which creates new lists at each recursive step. This results in **O(n) space complexity** (due to copied slices) and **O(log n) stack space**, contradicting the claimed O(1) space. The time complexity is also not strictly O(n) in the sense of a single pass; the slicing overhead adds up, though the total work remains linear. The explanation incorrectly states the space complexity and mischaracterizes the algorithm as a "single pass." Since the problem explicitly requires O(1) space, this is a significant flaw.

Rating: [[3]]
